correctness.rationale: For F subset of K_m square K_n, the number of F-neighbors of a missing cell (i,j) is d_i+e_j in the K_m,n incidence graph. Any cycle edge set is itself a fort, so a minimal fort containing a cycle must equal that cycle; square-board spanning cycles contain a proper perfect-matching fort, giving the sharp cyclic cap. An incidence forest has at most m+n-2 edges unless it spans as a tree, when deleting an internal edge preserves all row/column degrees positive and hence a smaller fort exists. An omitted-center two-arm cross has size m+n-2 and no proper nonempty subfort; when |m-n|=1, a 2min(m,n)-cycle omitting one column/row remains inclusion-minimal by forced degree-two propagation. Thus the formula holds for all m,n>=2. The independent finite DP checks every proper subset rather than just single deletions, and does not establish the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The rank (largest member size) of the fort obstruction hypergraph is a natural exact invariant distinct from fort packing and the number of minimal forts. Its complete two-parameter formula has a sharp one-cell exception for consecutive dimensions, with two structurally different extremal supports. It also characterizes the minimum cardinality of a maximal failed zero-forcing set by complement.

limitations: Only K_m square K_n rook graphs, m,n>=2; neither the number of minimal forts nor their complete classification is determined.
The independent exact proper-subset census tests seven boards; the universal theorem relies on the incidence-graph proof.
